transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just can’t get anything in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, senior-center notes, half-finished lists... and I sit there not knowing what to do first. Then the whole day is gone.
When did you first begin noticing this difficulty with getting organized and managing your tasks?
It’s been this bad for about a year and three months—since my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and daily arrangements.
Growing up or during your school years, did you struggle with staying organized and paying attention?
Yes. Even when I was little, my teachers would say I was bright but careless. I forgot my books and homework a lot, and they had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I could go outside.
Over the past month, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?
I’m not really sure. I’ve been overwhelmed, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed feeling down or hopeless all the time.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things, to the point where you have a hard time controlling it?
I’m not sure I’d call it worrying about lots of different things. I do feel overwhelmed sometimes, but I can’t really say it’s constant or hard to control.
Before your husband became ill, did you continue to have trouble throughout your adult life with things like staying organized, losing items, or focusing on tasks?

Yes, I did. I’ve had a hard time getting things in order for a long time. My table would end up covered in papers and lists, and I’d sit there not knowing what to start with. Then the day would be gone and I hadn’t gotten much done.
